title: The Chatbot Landscape
description: A clear map of the major AI chatbots — what each one is, who makes it, and when to use it.

data.text: There are now dozens of AI chatbots. But four dominate everyday use — ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Perplexity. Each has genuine strengths and real limitations. This lesson gives you a honest, practical map of each one so you can pick the right tool for the right job.
The four you need to know

cards.title: ChatGPT (OpenAI)
cards.description: The most widely used AI chatbot in the world. Made by OpenAI. The GPT-6 family powers it: GPT-6 Astra for hard reasoning, GPT-6.1 Sol as the everyday default, and GPT-6 Luna for fast responses. It handles text, images, audio, and can interpret charts and screenshots. Has the richest plugin and API ecosystem.
pros: Free tier with GPT-6 Luna access
cons: Context can degrade in very long chats

cards.title: Claude (Anthropic)
cards.description: Built by Anthropic, a safety-focused AI company. The Claude 5.5 family (Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Haiku 5.5) is known for nuanced, careful reasoning and handling very long documents. Its 1M-token context window means you can paste an entire book.
pros: Great at following complex multi-step instructions
cons: Can be overly cautious on edge-case requests

cards.title: Gemini (Google)
cards.description: Google's AI chatbot, deeply integrated into Google Workspace. Gemini 4 Argon handles complex work with a 1M-token context, while Gemini 3.8 Flash is the fast, lower-cost option. If you live in Gmail, Docs, and Drive, Gemini blends into your environment in ways other chatbots cannot. Strong real-time web access and multimodal understanding.
cons: Responses can be longer and less precise
Best features need Google AI Pro

cards.title: Perplexity
cards.description: An AI-powered search engine rather than a general chatbot. Every answer cites its sources. This dramatically reduces hallucination risk for factual questions. Think of it as Google + AI summary with footnotes.
pros: Every claim shows its source link
cons: Less useful for creative or coding tasks
Sources can still be wrong — verify important claims

rows: Editing or writing a long document
Handles up to 1M tokens in one go

data.text: How to choose a chatbot: practical criteria

items: Task fit: match the tool to the task (research vs. writing vs. workspace automation).
Context window: long documents need large context windows (Claude excels here).
Multimodality: if you need image or audio understanding, prefer multimodal models (ChatGPT, Gemini).
Integrations and APIs: choose tools that connect to your stack (ChatGPT plugins, Gemini with Google Workspace).
Transparency: for factual claims prefer tools that cite sources (Perplexity, Gemini with citations).
Cost and latency: weigh paid tiers for heavy usage; some features are paywalled.
Safety and compliance: consider data handling, enterprise controls, and audit logs for sensitive workflows.

data.text: Prompting tips tailored to each chatbot

rows: Use system messages and short examples; call the code interpreter for deterministic calculations.
System messages and examples help steer tone; code interpreter reduces arithmetic hallucinations.
Provide long context in one paste and ask for numbered steps or summaries.
Claude's long context window preserves document structure and reduces truncation.
Reference Drive/Docs explicitly and ask for actions (e.g., 'Create a draft in my Drive').
Gemini integrates with Workspace and can act on documents when permissions are granted.
Ask for concise answers and request source links for each factual claim.
Perplexity's strength is cited web evidence — use it to verify claims quickly.

data.text: Privacy, data handling, and enterprise controls

Different vendors have different default policies for data retention, training usage, and enterprise controls. For sensitive or regulated data, prefer enterprise offerings with explicit data residency, audit logs, and the ability to opt out of model training. Always read the vendor's privacy and security documentation before connecting production data.

rows: Does the vendor store prompts and responses?
Use enterprise plans or on-prem options; redact PII before sending
Will my data be used to improve models?
Choose plans that explicitly opt out of training or provide private instances
Can you restrict who can call write-capable tools?
Use least-privilege credentials and separate read/write keys
Are tool calls and outputs logged immutably?
Enable logging and export logs to your SIEM for compliance

data.text: How to evaluate chatbots for your use case

rows: Correctness of factual answers and extracted data
Does the model produce stable outputs for similar inputs?
Per-call or per-token cost at scale
Rate of unsafe or disallowed outputs
Critical for public-facing or regulated applications
Availability of APIs, plugins, and SDKs

data.title: Start strategy
data.text: Start with one tool — ChatGPT or Claude — and use it for 2 weeks across different tasks. Then add Perplexity for research. Most power users eventually run 2-3 tools for different jobs, not one tool for everything.

data.title: Research + write workflow
data.content: Use Perplexity to gather cited facts and links, then paste verified snippets into ChatGPT or Claude for synthesis and polished writing. Keep the citation list and raw sources in a shared doc for audit.

data.title: Workspace automation
data.content: Use Gemini for inbox triage and draft generation inside Gmail/Docs. Combine with a backend orchestrator to apply business rules and create calendar events or tasks automatically.

data.text: Pitfalls and limitations to watch for

No chatbot is perfect. Common issues include hallucinations (confident but incorrect statements), context loss in long conversations, inconsistent tone across sessions, and vendor-specific biases. For production use, add deterministic verification steps, human approval gates, and monitoring to catch drift.

data.title: Quick reference
points: ChatGPT — best overall, largest ecosystem, best free tier features
Claude — best for long documents, careful writing, complex instructions
Gemini — best with Google Workspace and for real-time web
Perplexity — best for factual research that needs cited sources
Most professionals use 2-3 tools — not one for everything
